title: Thrifty Feed: Sweet Potato Dhal
subtitle: Budget-busting tummy fillers!
description: Filling, tried-and-true flavours, and even more budget-friendly than our core menu – that’s our Thrifty Feed recipes! These classic dishes are perfect for when you want to put tasty, honest-to-goodness dinners on the table, and enjoy even more savings to boot.

steps.text: Cook garlic rice: Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Rinse rice until water runs clear. Heat 1 tbs vegetable oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook the garlic, stirring, for 30 secs, then stir in the rice. Add 250ml (1 cup) water, cover and bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low and cook for 12 mins or until the water is absorbed. Turn off the heat and stand, covered, for at least 5 mins.

Start dhal: Meanwhile, finely chop the onion. Peel and coarsely grate the sweet potato. Heat 1 tbs vegetable oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion, stirring, for 3-4 mins until softened. Add the sweet potato and 2 tbs water and cook, stirring, for 5-6 mins until the sweet potato is starting to soften.

Add lentils: Add the masala seasoning and half the tomato paste to the vegetables and cook, stirring, for 1 min or until fragrant. Stir in the lentils, coconut milk and 250ml (1 cup) water, season with pepper and bring to the boil.

Simmer dhal: Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover the dhal and cook, stirring occasionally, for 18 mins or until the lentils and sweet potato are broken down. Add the spinach and cook, stirring, for 30 secs or until wilted. Remove the pan from the heat and stand, covered, for 3 mins (see Cooking tip).

Serve up: Add 1 tsp white wine vinegar and 1 tsp honey to the dhal and stir to combine. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Fluff the rice with a fork. Divide the garlic rice and dhal among bowls and enjoy!
Make it herby: If you have some on hand in the crisper drawer or veggie garden, scatter some chopped coriander or parsley over the dhal for a burst of freshness.
